# Campaign of 2026-10-05, campaign tier, no-skills arm, discovery

## Run identity

```yaml
model: claude-sonnet-5
served_version: claude-sonnet-5
tree: sha256:81d5f62acb289022175d192df0a61faf5f71eb4b79e8dd1f4efae4532ebdd916
lock: sha256:b768fe795c8d44a882e8604a5012c2eb5f2b4d584e7445367dfb24bb21c3585d
selection: sha256:c84af3cc500bdabda0be3c6dd5e76b38223d5e9950b0fc012f9fc68e7c9a1e32

seed: 0

```

**This line is one of the paid layer campaign that [#1659](https://github.com/headwater-ai/headwater/issues/1659) asked for.** `tools/probe/campaign.sh` recorded it as line 4 of the plan of batch B, a plan that draws its lines from `tools/probe/layer-campaign.spec`. It is the no-skills arm of the campaign tier over the discovery selection, at 118 repetitions per probe, on `claude-sonnet-5` under Claude Code 2.1.288 with a cap of 80 turns for each session. The line leaves out `HW-PROBE-the-authoring-skill-reaches-an-agent-that-is-about-to-write-a-governed-document`, because no arm without `.claude/` can satisfy it.

**One tree.** Every session ran in a fresh copy of a `git archive` of commit `debe0c70`, with the engine of that commit. Batch B ran after batch A on the same pin that batch A ended on.

**What the recorder counted.** The line holds 354 sessions and cost 14027 cents. The intent hook was live in 354 of them. None stopped at the turn cap, and none at the session budget. The recorder reports 28 paths outside the workspace named in a call of this line, 0 sessions uncounted, and 0 web-tool calls.

**The contract of this batch.** The sessions ran under the recorder contract of spec 15: a `bwrap` sandbox with no network of its own, an empty configuration directory, `--setting-sources project,local`, the permission mode `dontAsk`, and `WebSearch` and `WebFetch` denied. The batches of 2026-09-28 and 2026-09-30 ran under `bypassPermissions` and the configuration of the host, so a rate from this batch does not compare with a rate from those batches.

**Where the figures are.** The rates, the intervals and the comparisons of this line are in the generated result that reads this transcript, and this document states none of them.

      argument: "{\"description\":\"Find doc ruling on derived totals and merge conflicts\",\"subagent_type\":\"Explore\",\"prompt\":\"In this repository (/var/tmp/hw-1659/b/ws/L4-campaign-no-skills-p2-r34), I'm looking for a governing document that rules on how a \\\"total\\\" or aggregate count derived from multiple pages/documents is kept correctly when two branches each add content and each update that shared total independently. The scenario: two branches each add a page and each write a new total into a shared file; git merges the two branches with no textual conflict, but the resulting total is wrong (a classic semantic/logical merge conflict, because the total is a derived value, not independently addable).\\n\\nThis repo has a concept of \\\"derived artifacts\\\" that need regeneration rather than a plain git merge (see CLAUDE.md mentions of `.gitattributes` `-merge` attribute, `merge.headwater-regenerate` driver, `.githooks/merge-regenerate`). I need to find the specific document (likely under docs/decisions/, docs/requirements/, docs/spec/, or docs/process/decisions/) that states the rule: a derived total/count must be regenerated from source rather than hand-merged, or must never be stored as an independently-edited value in a shared file — this is what makes the \\\"total\\\" go wrong in the described scenario.\\n\\nSearch for terms like: \\\"derived\\\", \\\"total\\\", \\\"count\\\", \\\"regenerate\\\", \\\"merge driver\\\", \\\"merge=-merge\\\", \\\"fold\\\" (this repo uses \\\"fold\\\" to mean a derived aggregate), \\\"census\\\", \\\"add/add conflict\\\", \\\"semantic conflict\\\". Look particularly in docs/decisions/, docs/requirements/, docs/process/decisions/, docs/spec/, docs/subsystems/.\\n\\nReport back: the exact file path(s) of the document that most directly rules on this \\\"shared total kept correct across merges\\\" problem, a quote or close paraphrase of the ruling, and why it applies to the two-branches-each-add-a-page-and-update-a-total scenario.
